items.prompt: Name one of the four factors of natural selection.
items.answer: Overproduction of offspring (or heritable variation, competition, or more reproduction of better-suited individuals)

steps: The four factors drive natural selection.

items.prompt: What does heritable variation provide for natural selection?
items.answer: Differences among individuals that can be passed on

steps: Variation gives selection something to act on.

items.prompt: Which individuals tend to survive and reproduce more?
items.answer: Those with traits better suited to the environment

items.prompt: Do populations tend to produce more offspring than can survive?

steps: Overproduction is one of the four factors.

items.prompt: What happens to helpful traits over generations?

steps: Helpful traits spread through the population.

items.prompt: Better-camouflaged beetles survive better. What becomes more common over time?

steps: The surviving trait spreads over generations.

items.prompt: Is natural selection the main process driving evolution?
What must a trait be for natural selection to pass it on?

steps: Only heritable traits can be passed on.

items.prompt: Faster rabbits escape predators better. What becomes more common?
Explain why heritable variation is necessary for natural selection.
items.answer: Selection needs heritable differences to act on and pass to offspring

steps: Without variation there is nothing to select.

items.prompt: Explain how camouflage becomes common in a beetle population.
items.answer: Better-camouflaged beetles survive and reproduce more, passing on camouflage over generations

steps: The surviving trait spreads over generations.

items.prompt: Why do more offspring being produced than can survive matter?
items.answer: It creates competition, so only some survive to reproduce

items.prompt: Construct an explanation for antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
items.answer: A few resistant bacteria survive the antibiotic and reproduce, so resistance spreads over generations

items.prompt: List the four factors of natural selection.
items.answer: Overproduction, heritable variation, competition for limited resources, and more reproduction of better-suited individuals

steps: These four factors drive natural selection.
